pageCache.pageTitle: Queens Gate School for Girls aged 4-18, in South Kensington
pageCache.text:
WELCOME Welcome
It is my pleasure to welcome you to Queen’s Gate School. We are a day school for girls aged 4-18, located in South Kensington, in the centre of London’s educational and cultural heartland, the perfect place to inspire and indulge young hearts and minds. Our close-knit community is a special one. Our central London home affords us a diverse, multinational intake, and our size allows us to know every girl as an individual.
Start yourQGS journey
JUNIOR SCHOOL
At Queen’s Gate, our girls enjoy a broad and stimulating education within a nurturing environment. They are happy, secure in their learning and prepared to make bold choices. Our ethos is underpinned by the belief that every child is an individual.
SENIOR SCHOOL
Our Senior School provides a bright, positive and aspirational atmosphere. Girls are encouraged and supported to achieve at the highest level they can, and to throw themselves in all that we offer.
OUR LOCATION LONDON IS OUR PLAYGROUND
As a Central London school, Queen’s Gate is ideally situated to take advantage of the wealth of facilities in our local area. For sport we enjoy the use of Hyde Park, Battersea Park and several top-class leisure centres and pools. School trips regularly visit the nearby Natural History Museum, V&A Museum, Science Museum and Royal Geographic Society. With the bright lights of London’s West End and Southbank just a short tube ride away, our girls enjoy regular visits to the theatre.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mission Statement & Aims | Prep School London | Queen's Gate School
pageCache.text:
Mission Statement & Aims
At Queen’s Gate, our mission is to offer an education for life in a stimulating environment where sound values and individuality are nurtured within a supportive atmosphere.
Our aim is for every girl not only to realise her potential, but to exceed it. We achieve this through encouraging each girl to adopt an aspirational, growth mindset and by fostering an atmosphere where self-motivation and self-confidence are key. Alongside this, we provide close, individualised support, using our knowledge of each individual pupil, as well as her baseline data, to provide feedback and guidance that is truly relevant to her. We seek to instil a love of learning through engaging, innovative lessons while actively seeking to strengthen each girl’s self-confidence and self-esteem, qualities we know will support intellectual risk-taking and resilience.
We are proudly holistic in our ethos, promoting co-curricular involvement and the development of strong values-based character traits. We aim for our girls to have every opportunity to discover, develop and demonstrate her own gifts and talents, and to feel valued for what she personally brings to our community – and those around us. Since our foundation, Queen’s Gate has been dedicated to thinking of those less fortunate than ourselves, both near and far, and facilitate a wide range of charitable and outreach activities. A genuine generosity of spirit underpins all that we do, and makes our school a truly rewarding place to be.
We revel in our originality, encouraging fearless creativity and embracing the notion of authenticity. We wish for each girl to have the opportunity to be her true self, to feel empowered to pursue her own interests and inspired to challenge and explore. We are unashamed in our promotion of a positive, good-humoured atmosphere in which joy and laughter are ever-present, for we believe that the happiest girls are those who are most likely to over-achieve, in their academic endeavours, their co-curricular interests and their own personal development.

About Us
Queen’s Gate School is an independent school for girls aged 4-18 located on Queen’s Gate, in South Kensington, London. Founded in 1891, the school has long held a reputation for its originality. Our fundamental goal is that each girl should become the very best version of herself, making the most of her individual strengths, gifts and talents. Our girls hold themselves and each other to high standards, but always with a lightness of heart. At Queen’s Gate, we are not afraid to laugh at ourselves.
Queen’s Gate is an academically aspirational school, where we seek for each girl to go beyond her individual academic potential. We have no one-size-fits-all definition of success; rather, we provide the guidance and conditions for each girl to reach beyond what she might have thought possible. At Queen’s Gate, we aim to be a greenhouse rather than a hothouse – deliberately cultivating a supportive, collaborative and positive atmosphere, governed by our belief that happy girls are more likely to overachieve.
Academic Excellence and Value-Added Success
Our academic results are excellent: every year, countless girls are successful in attaining straight 8/9 grades at GCSE and A/A* at A level. However, our priority is that each girl should feel valued for the effort she has put in, and the progress she has made. We know there will be lower grades that have been just as hard won – if not more so – and we are determined that those girls should be celebrated, both for the determination they have shown, and the many other gifts and talents they offer our community.
Our success in supporting each girl to exceed her potential is proven by our incredible value-added scores, measures of how far beyond her baseline potential each girl has gone. Here, we are consistently placed among the top-ten schools in the country, proof of what Queen’s Gate enables our girls to achieve.
Outstanding University Destinations
University destinations are as varied and individual as our girls. We are able to boast of girls attending top UK universities, including Oxford and Cambridge, as well as overseas institutions such as Harvard and NYU. We have an incredibly strong record of sending girls onto some of the most elite art schools in the world, including Central St. Martins, Camberwell School of Art and Parsons School of Design (New York). With our strength in STEM subjects, many of our girls have gone on to courses such as Computer Science at St. Andrews, Mechanical Engineering at UCL and Creative Computing at the University of the Arts, London.
London as our Extended Campus
Housed in five of the iconic Victorian mansions that dominate South Kensington, we are ideally situated to take advantage of the nearby museums, Royal Albert Hall, Royal Academy of Music, and many parks and sporting facilities. Girls are able to pop into the Victoria & Albert Museum during a normal timetabled lesson, visit the Natural History Museum as a lunchtime club, and jump on the tube to reach the theatres of the West End and Southbank. London really is our playground, offering endless opportunities to extend our girls’ academic learning, enrich our co-curricular offering and enhance their personal development.
Personalised Teaching and Small School Community
As a smaller school, the staff at Queen’s Gate are truly able to get to know our girls as the individuals they are. Learning is more of a partnership between teacher and pupil, with close, personalised support throughout her academic journey with us. Our staff demonstrate their dedication through consistent provision of extra lunchtime clinics and holiday revision classes, designed to enable all learners to embark upon assessments and exams feeling as confident as possible.
Pastoral Care and Wellbeing
The wellbeing of our pupils guides us in all aspects of school life. High-quality pastoral care and the safeguarding of pupils underpin everything that we do. Our PSHE programme is regularly reviewed to ensure we are meeting the needs of our girls, while the strong staff-pupil relationships mean girls feel safe to come forward and share worries.
A Broad and Inspiring Co-Curricular Programme
Our co-curricular programme is broad and forward-thinking, spanning super-curricular options, creative activities and those choices that are simply there for fun and to give girls a space where they can relax and feel they belong. Music, Drama and Sport are all well-represented, while pupil voice is central, with girls having the opportunity to serve on a number of committees dedicated to giving them a forum in which to put forward ideas and share feedback. As we work to tackle societal gender inequality, it is especially important to us to encourage our girls to learn how to use their voices, and not hold back from sharing their ideas.
A Diverse and Inclusive London Community
As a cosmopolitan, central London community, we are naturally multinational and multifaith. Celebrating all our cultural traditions, including religious festivals, provides a rich environment for our girls to discover and explore the values of diversity and respect. All share in each other’s traditions, whether that’s Lunar New Year, Hanukkah, Ramadan or our Christian festivals, and embrace the meaning of inclusion. Families of all backgrounds enjoy gatherings such as our Carol Service, welcoming warmly the reflective, thoughtful and welcoming atmosphere we create.
It is our insistence on providing an experience that goes beyond pure academic education that our families most value. Our aim is for each girl to become the best version of herself – as a learner, as a friend, as a leader and as a future citizen.
Visitors routinely comment on how natural our girls are and how generously they welcome guests to the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Principal | Queen's Gate School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Principal
It is my pleasure to welcome you to Queen’s Gate. We are a day school for girls aged 4-18, located in South Kensington, on the edge of the capital’s educational and cultural heartland, the perfect place to inspire and indulge young hearts and minds. Our close-knit community of around 500 pupils is a special one. Our central London home affords us a diverse, multinational intake, our size allows us to know every girl as an individual, and our desire to feel ‘unschooly’ is brought to life in touches such as our lack of uniform.
We are unashamedly proud of our pupils’ many successes. We aim to provide a learning environment in which girls feel enabled and empowered to stretch themselves both intellectually and personally. We seek for each of our girls to develop a lifelong love of learning: a readiness to question, an appetite for knowledge and the self-belief that they will find their way through any challenge. Alongside this, in line with our core values, we encourage character traits of compassion and consideration, respect and integrity. We delight in the authenticity we see emerge in our girls, their confidence to be their true selves and their enjoyment of discovering, developing and demonstrating their own personal gifts and talents.
Throughout this website you will find evidence of our achievement of our aims, whether that is the list of schools our Junior School girls go onto for their secondary education, details of our extra-curricular programme, news items on recent speakers or a compendium of our Upper Sixth leavers’ destinations. However, a website can never truly convey the spirit and warmth to be found inside our Victorian walls, and so I would very much welcome you and your daughter to take advantage of one of our open events or book a private tour to see for yourself what Queen’s Gate is all about. We are so looking forward to meeting you.
Lydia Kyle is an experienced educational leader with over 16 years of teaching across both standalone preparatory and all-through schools. She began her career in a standalone prep school before moving into all-through settings, where she has developed a clear and informed vision of what a cohesive, all-through education can offer pupils. Her experience spans a range of contexts, including a short period in the state sector, giving her a broad and balanced perspective on education in the UK.

Governors
Chair - Mrs Reica Gray
A Queen’s Gate alumna, Reica enjoyed a two-decade career in professional theatre, progressing from stage manager to director of a major London theatre chain. Later, she pursued her passion for English, completing a BA and MA, then going on to manage an Academic Writing Centre at the university’s School of Business and Law. A keen writer, she is completing a novel set in the world of early twentieth century music hall, due for publication later this year.
Mr Paul Baldwin
Paul started his career in international corporate tax at Arthur Andersen in 1996. For the last 25 years he has focussed on M&A, and the latter 20 specialising in restructuring, refinancing and corporate insolvency.
Outside of work, Paul has been heavily involved in domestic rowing; various administrative offices and several treasurer roles both locally and regionally, an event organiser, as well as a commentator at Henley Royal Regatta, and formerly a multi-lane umpire. Paul is currently a trustee of a West London rowing charity. Paul is also involved in the Livery, being a freeman of both the Worshipful Company of Wheelwrights and the Company of Watermen & Lightermen of the River Thames.
Paul lives in Wandsworth and has a MEng from Imperial College.
Ms Nicola Bright
With a background of 30+ years in senior roles in education, Nicky was the Head of an all-through Girls’ Schools Association (GSA) boarding school, and Deputy of both a girls’ London day school and boarding school in Wiltshire. She was a member of the GSA governing council, chairing the GSA’s Professional Development Committee, an ISI inspector and a member of the BSA’s expert panel. Now a leadership development facilitator and coach, Nicky works with clients in a variety of different industries running leadership development programmes and coaching teams and individual leaders, and runs senior and middle leader group coaching programmes for the GSA. Nicky lives in London and enjoys the wide variety of artistic and cultural opportunities that brings.
Miss Karen Coles
Headmistress of Sarum Hall School with over 25 years’ experience in the independent sector since graduating from Exeter University with a BEd (Hons) degree in education. Having worked at Port Regis, Fulham Prep, Cheam and St George’s Weybridge, Karen has a long history of working with top senior schools to recommend them to her prep school parents. A serving Army Reserve Officer in the Intelligence Corps, Karen is also an accomplished swimmer, skier and tennis player so champions the importance of sport and working with others to achieve a collective goal.
Ms Carol Davis KC
Following her degree in English Literature, Carol headed to the Bar. Since being called to the Bar in 1996, Carol has practised from Littleton Chambers in London. She specialises in Employment litigation and professional discipline. She has a recognised expertise in discrimination law and high-value Employment Tribunal litigation, commercial employment matters in the High Court and regulatory work, with a particular emphasis on financial services, education, and healthcare. Carol was appointed a Queen’s Counsel in 2021. Carol lives in London with her husband, two daughters and an assortment of pets.
Mrs Emma Ghosh
Mr Shai Hill
Shai began his career on the buyside at what is now JP Morgan AM, before moving to the sellside where he worked in several research roles. He was Head of Research at Macquarie Group for 10 years before founding lntegrum ESG in 2018. Shai has an M.A. in English from Cambridge University.
Mrs Clare Lenterman
Clare grew up in France, returning to the UK for Sixth Form and University. She has a BA Hons in Modern Languages (French and Italian). She worked for 6 years in the Equities Division at Goldman Sachs, London, in sales and trading compliance. Clare and her Dutch husband are parents to 6 children. Their youngest daughter attends Queen’s Gate School and is currently in Lower Sixth. The family spent a total of 16 years living in Amsterdam, where Clare was actively involved in the children’s schools, in particular the International School of Amsterdam (ISA) where she served on the Board of Trustees from 2013–2016, (Board Secretary, Governance Chair) as well as running the PTA for a total of 4 years. In 2022, Clare spent 6 months working at ISA developing and implementing their staW Code of Conduct, and safeguarding policies, as well as overseeing and monitoring relevant staW safeguarding training including the use of the CPOMS platform.
Clare is passionate about education, with a strong interest in theatre. An avid sewer and designer, for the past 20 years, she has had a small business designing, making and sourcing costumes for school theatre productions. She has especially enjoyed working with Queen’s Gate Junior School since 2016 on their annual musical theatre production.
Mr David Sharman
Mr Simon Underwood
Simon lives in Barnes having spent his working life in London. His insolvency career spans 35+ years. He was President of the Insolvency Practitioners Association in 2007 / 2008 and is currently a Board Member. He has served on Menzies’ Management Committee and was the Managing Partner of the Business Recovery and then the Transaction Services team, which included Business Recovery, Forensic Services and Corporate Finance. He is the Immediate Past Master of the Worshipful Company of Arbitrators. Historically, he was active within the Livery Schools Link Committee, developing close relationships with Clara Grant Primary School, delivering a financial literacy program. He is married to Amanda. They have been together for over 25 years and enjoy travelling, particularly scuba-diving adventures. Additionally, he enjoys cycling, skiing and camping, which have yet to appeal to Amanda!

pageCache.pageTitle: How To Reach Us | Queen's Gate School
pageCache.text:
How to Reach Us
Queen’s Gate School is located on Queen’s Gate, in South Kensington, London. We are one block away from the Natural History Museum, and close to Imperial College, the Victoria & Albert Museum and the Royal Albert Hall.
To reach us by public transport, please use the District, Circle or Piccadilly Underground lines to reach Gloucester Road or South Kensington Stations; we are a mere five minute walk from each. A number of TfL public buses also stop nearby.
Parking on Queen’s Gate is limited, but there are a number of public car parks in the nearby area.
Visitors to the Junior School should make their way to 126 Queen’s Gate, while those seeking the Senior School should come to 133 Queen’s Gate.
We look forward to welcoming you.
Junior School
Senior School

ISI Reports
Queen’s Gate School was delighted to host representatives from the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) in November 2024. The opportunity to show off all that makes our school so special had been hotly awaited, and both staff and pupils welcomed our guests most warmly.
Under the ISI framework in place since 2023, schools no longer receive overall judgements such as ‘excellent’. Rather, the inspectors report on whether a school meets the expected ISI standards in five key areas:
1. Leadership and management, and governance
2. Quality of education, training and recreation
3. Pupils’ physical and mental health and emotional wellbeing
4. Pupils’ social and economic education and contribution to society
At our November inspection, Queen’s Gate School was successful in meeting the standards in every area, while the overall report (available below) gives us just cause to use one of our favourite phrases, ‘unashamedly proud’.
It is fair to say that our visitors really were able to capture all that makes our School so special. Our guiding principles around pupil wellbeing, and about each girl being encouraged to become her own personal best are both noted. “Pupils are at the heart of leaders’ decision making” is a genuine reflection of how we do things at Queen’s Gate. Every choice we make, every development we advance, is done with our girls’ needs in mind. Within this, we strive for each girl to exceed her potential, her own personal best: our vision is described as “ambitious for every pupil to develop fully whatever their starting point” and “based around developing the individual within a supportive school environment.”
As well as confirming that we had met both our targets from the previous inspection, which centred on our use of digital technology in learning and our quality of marking and feedback, our visitors found much to praise in our teaching provision. “Teachers skilfully adapt lessons to the needs of pupils and respond to their interests and questions.” “Teachers throughout the school use their extensive subject knowledge to teach well-planned lessons which enable pupils to extend their knowledge and deepen their understanding.” The curriculum is described as “diverse and ambitious.”
Throughout the visit, our Queen’s Gate girls truly shone, showing deep pride in, and loyalty towards, the School. With their natural self-confidence and open-hearted generosity of spirit, they took enormous pleasure in welcoming our guests. In particular, the inspectors noted the quality of relationships between pupils and staff, commenting “Relationships between pupils and staff are positive across the school. Pupils feel respected and they in turn respect each other. Staff are caring and interested in pupils’ wellbeing and their success…Pupils feel they are valued.” Similarly pleasing is the line “Leaders have established a school culture and curriculum which fosters understanding and celebrates diversity.” We consider ourselves exceptionally lucky to enjoy a school community that comprises many ethnicities, faiths and cultures. Our pupils gain a sophisticated understanding of the world, and a deep-rooted respect for different perspectives and values.
All schools receive at least one recommendation. This time we have received just one recommendation, and work has already started towards this. We can’t wait to see what we can achieve.

pageCache.pageTitle: Junior School Pastoral Care - Queen's Gate School
pageCache.text:
Junior School Pastoral Care
In keeping with our whole-school ethos, at Queen’s Gate Junior School we are renowned for our exceptional pastoral care. We understand that the wellbeing of our girls is fundamental to their school experiences, their ability to make strong academic and personal progress, and their readiness for the future.
Queen’s Gate Junior School is small in size, with just one class for each year, enabling us to give our pupils a great deal of individual attention. Our family ethos ensures that each child is valued and nurtured; support and extension derive naturally from the close relationships that are built.
Queen’s Gate has access to a private green space at Stanhope Gardens, which is a four minute walk from the School. Girls can enjoy daily fresh air and a chance to run around during break time. Our co-curricular programme provides rich opportunities for happiness and collaboration whether it be through dance, food technology, mindfulness or art.
House System
Our House system enables us to provide an additional support network based on vertical integration within the School.
Membership of Victoria and Elizabeth Houses provides the opportunity for older and younger girls to collaborate closely and fosters healthy competition at events such as Sports Day, our Recycled Fashion Show, and our Christmastime ‘Winter Games’. This eclectic range of activities allows all girls to find their moment to shine. The Houses are led by two Year 6 House Captains, and House spirit is fierce – as anyone who has heard the cheering at the Swimming Gala will confirm.
Celebrations of Success
Personal success is celebrated on a regular basis, and the annual Celebration of the Year event provides the opportunity for parents to share in our girls’ achievements.
‘Merits’ are highly-valued rewards and are awarded not only for excellence but also for effort and kindness. Our twice-weekly morning assemblies provide another opportunity to promote achievement, whether that’s through our ‘Sports Star of the Week’ certificates, or by announcing that a pupil has won a competition outside of school. Our WHAM (Wellbeing, Happiness, Achievement and Motivation) assemblies on Friday afternoons are a joyous celebration of the girls’ successes and provide a wonderfully uplifting note on which to end the week.
Each term ends with two special assemblies, one dedicated the awarding of sports certificates and colours, and the other to the girls’ other successes. Academic certificates and prizes are awarded both for attainment and progress, to ensure all girls feel valued and celebrated as learners.
Wellbeing
Queen’s Gate Junior School girls are happy and self-reflective. The promotion of wellbeing and positive emotional and mental health underpins every decision we make at Queen’s Gate Junior School. Our specialist PSHE programme is designed to support the girls at every step of their journey through childhood and prepare them for the years to come. Being part of a through-school, we have the particular advantage of being able to liaise with colleagues in the Senior School and use their experiences to inform what we are delivering to our Junior School pupils, so they are as ready as possible for their teenage years. As well as regular PSHE lessons, we also enjoy an annual Wellbeing Week, individual ‘drop down’ days with outside specialists and regularly touch on the theme of wellbeing in our assemblies.
Our Relationships and Sex Education Programme is delivered as part of our PSHE provision. These lessons have been carefully designed to be fully age appropriate, while ensuring our girls are gaining the knowledge and understanding they need. Parents are always provided with full information ahead of any RSE lessons, and are given the opportunity to discuss the content with staff in advance.
That partnership with parents is something we develop further through our schedule of engaging and thought-provoking termly workshops. Parent feedback on topics they would like us to cover is always warmly welcomed.

Drama
Queen’s Gate School Drama is a thriving part of the school, where our girls get the opportunity to explore all aspects of theatrical production. We our proud to have a number of extremely talented and well-known actors among our alumnae, whose work inspires the next generation of Queen’s Gate girls.
As well as the curricular and co-curricular drama detailed below, the department has its own specialised LAMDA teacher who offers lessons to girls throughout the school. We are proud to boast a 100% pass rate, with girls securing enviable results at all levels.
Invested in guiding girls at every stage of their theatrical journey, our aim is to nurture a lifelong love of Drama and Theatre.
Junior School
Queen’s Gate girls love to perform! Individual music lessons in a wide variety of instruments are available, as well as choirs and orchestras to join. Many performances take place during the year.
I love the school play because it taught us how real theatres work!
An appreciation of the Arts is evident throughout the school. Music and Drama are highly prized for their intrinsic value and for the part they play in the personal development of each child.
Senior School
In Years 7 to 9, Queen’s Gate girls develop their knowledge and understanding of key dramatic techniques. They explore a wide range of theatrical styles and examine a diverse variety of texts as both performers and designers. Teachers create a fun and supportive environment where girls are encouraged to take creative risks from the onset.
At GCSE girls develop and refine their skills in devising and performance. They become adept at analysing and evaluating live theatre and enjoy exploring their prescribed text in practical workshops. Those who wish to extend their skill set go on to study GCE Drama and Theatre Studies. At this level the methodology of two influential theatre practitioners is applied in the practical components, whilst two contrasting texts and a live theatre production are studied for the written examination.
Outside of curricular time our dedicated Drama studio, which boasts its own lighting and sound system, is a hive of activity. Budding performers extend their acting skills at Remove Drama Society or as a member of The Arthur Players. Inspired by the success of past alumni, girls relish the opportunity to perform on stage. The annual Senior School production is undoubtedly a highlight of the academic year and the high standards achieved are a testament to our girls’ talent and hard work. Professional lighting together with costumes hired from ‘The National Theatre’ add that extra sprinkle of magic! Recent productions include, ’Oh What a Lovely War’, ‘Great Expectations’ and ‘The 39 Steps’. We firmly believe in empowering our fledgling directors and once a year LVI take the reins, auditioning and directing girls in The LIV Play.
Taking advantage of our close proximity to the West End, girls benefit from watching work created by leading theatre makers. Workshops led by practitioners from renowned Theatre Companies also motivate and encourage girls to find new ways of communicating meaning to an audience.

Music
Music at Queen’s Gate School aims to play an invaluable role in the development of each and every pupil, enriching the lives of all who come to our school. We encourage and enthuse those of all abilities, with enjoyment and excellence at the heart of our provision.
We offer an engaging and practical syllabus, from our youngest pupils in Preliminary right up to A level, with specialist teachers throughout the Junior and Senior School.
Over half our girls have instrumental lessons with a broad range of instruments on offer, including singing, harp and drum kit.
We have many thriving musical ensembles and choirs that rehearse weekly. Ranging from Chamber Choirs who annually are asked to lead the charity Kids for Kids Christmas Concert, to our rock bands who always perform in each term’s Senior School final assembly, we make sure we have something for every pupil, whatever her level of musical experience or proficiency. Our Junior School puts on a musical each year and we have our highly contested House Music Competition annually.
The music department regularly puts on performance opportunities. Individual performances in assemblies and instrument-specific teatime recitals provide girls with the opportunity to build confidence in a more relaxed setting. We also hold much larger end-of-term concerts featuring a range of solo and ensemble performances. Our 130th Anniversary concert involved over 80 girls performing alongside a professional orchestra. Girls also take advantage of the wonderful opportunities to see and hear professional concerts and shows at a range of London venues.

Parents’ Association
Queen’s Gate School is very fortunate to benefit from the loyal and tireless support of its Parents’ Association. The PTA has wings for the Junior School and Senior School, and is formed of parent Class Representatives from every year group. These two wings arrange activities throughout the year for the parents and pupils in their section of the school, as well as joining together for whole-school events. The money raised is donated by the Parents’ Association towards specific projects they wish to support, or to gift one-off items.
The Parents’ Association’s major event each year is our Christmas Fair, a highlight of our festive season and always a huge success. Other activities include drinks parties and our very popular and hotly-contested quiz nights. The Junior School PTA kindly arrange a number of activities for the younger pupils, including our annual Easter egg hunt.
New or current parents wishing to get involved in the Queen’s Gate School Parents’ Association are invited to share their contact details upon joining the school. The Parents’ Association can also be contacted through the School Office who will be pleased to forward on any messages.

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior School Pastoral Care - Queen's Gate School
pageCache.text:
Senior School Pastoral Care
Pupil wellbeing is central to life at Queen’s Gate and strong pupil and teacher relationships, where teachers know every pupil as an individual, are the foundations of our pastoral care structure. We believe firmly that positive self-esteem and a sense of feeling happy and well cared for are fundamental for pupil progress, both in terms of their academic attainment and their personal development.
Staffing
At Queen’s Gate, all staff see themselves as having a key role in supporting the pastoral care of our pupils. However, a number of roles have particular pastoral responsibilities, together providing truly holistic care for our girls.
Form Tutors see girls in the morning and at afternoon registration and will usually be the first port of call for girls and parents. Weekly Form Time sessions allow Form Tutors and pupils to explore.
All year groups benefit from a Head of Year and Deputy Head of Year who oversee both the well-being and academic progress of the girls in their care. These staff are responsible for identifying key issues for their specific age group and responding where girls might be experiencing difficulties. They also lead regular year group assemblies, again focusing on topics that are of particular relevance to the girls in their cohort.
At Queen’s Gate, SEND provision comes under the auspices of our Learning Support Department. Their work is crucial for the girls’ academic progress, as well as playing an important part in the well-being of our girls. The Learning Support Department liaises closely with our subject and pastoral staff, to ensure that any difficulties are recognised and supported in the best way possible. We also offer specialist EAL tuition which is invaluable for those girls for whom English is not their first language.
Our School Counsellors visit the school each week and are available to offer extra support for pupils who need an extra listening ear. We are also able to offer 1:1 coaching for girls who may appreciate some extra help with specific issues such as exam anxiety or difficulties managing relationships with peers.
Pastoral care at Queen’s Gate Senior School is overseen by the Director of Pastoral Care. Together the pastoral team plans a programme of proactive support, which seeks to meet the needs of the girls before issues can arise. Experts in working with adolescent girls, they keep up-to-date with trends and research, ensuring the provision of forward-thinking, modern and relevant pastoral care.
PSHE
Queen’s Gate is committed to an education that truly prepares our girls to flourish in the wider world. We aim to provide an exciting, practical and relevant PSHE curriculum, allowing girls to explore challenges that they may face in real life in the calm of their Queen’s Gate classrooms. There is no such thing as a typical PSHE lesson at Queen’s Gate and girls will find themselves discussing a wide range of topics from holiday safety and healthy eating to the ethics of advertising or the relationship conundrums in their recent favourite Netflix series. The content of Personal, Social and Health Education sessions at Queen’s Gate, as well as the Relationship and Sex Education curriculum are informed by pupil voice, as well as statutory government requirements, to ensure that sessions really are relevant and meeting pupil needs.
Parent Seminars
At Queen’s Gate we are keen to work in partnership with families to support the wellbeing of our pupils. For this reason we have a programme of Parent Seminars which aim to support parents in understanding their children and the different stages of their development, as well as helping parents to navigate tricky issues such as teenage friendship, social media and the party scene – and the challenge of how to conduct productive conversations about these topics. We always welcome suggestions for new seminars, and our programme is constantly evolving to meet the changing needs of our parent body.
Pupil Voice
Accessing the views of pupils is extremely important to us at Queen’s Gate. Pupils can represent the views of their form on School Council and Food Committee, and this year we will be introducing an Environmental Committee. Our Prefect Team take the lead on pupil voice, chairing a number of these committees, a well as meeting weekly with the Principal to put forward suggestions and discuss current issues. Queen’s Gate also seeks to obtain pupil feedback through regular surveys on issues such as PSHE, dress code, the curriculum and school trips.
House System
Girls belong to one of our four Houses which allows them to meet and work with girls in other year groups, as well as enjoy an extra special sense of belonging. Rivalry between the four can only be described as fierce, as can be seen at events such as our Swimming Gala. Competition ranges across sports, music, drama and debating, to name just a few, with new suggestions always welcome.
Assemblies
Full school assemblies are held twice a week and offer the opportunity for the Queen’s Gate community to come together to reflect on spiritual and moral issues or world events as well as celebrating our successes. Our Readings, prayers and music recognise a range of spiritual approaches and philosophies and there are opportunities for individual pupils and forms to be involved in presenting and preparing assemblies.
Mobile Phone Policy
Queen’s Gate hopes that all our pupils will leave understanding how to manage their use of mobile phones and similar devices in a way that is positive, purposeful and healthy. To this end, we are proud to be a Yondr school, whereby pupils in Remove (Year 7) to Form V (Year 10) are asked to lock their phones in a specially designed pouch each morning. This allows them the security of keeping their phone on their person throughout the day, but without being able to use it, encouraging them instead to focus on face-to-face interactions with their peers and staff. Prospective and current parents with queries about how the management of mobile phones are warmly encouraged to get in touch with the Director of Pastoral Care.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sixth Form Pastoral Care - Queen's Gate School
pageCache.text:
Sixth Form Pastoral Care
Sixth Form life at Queen’s Gate is based on strong and respectful relationships between staff and students. Sixth Form students play an important role in the life of Queen’s Gate, working closely with teachers in their roles as prefects, Sixth Form Sisters to younger pupils, Peer Mentors as well as running clubs and societies.
At Queen’s Gate we appreciate that our Sixth Form pupils may have different wellbeing needs to those of our younger pupils. Every Sixth Former has a Work Tutor with whom she has 1:1 sessions to discuss study, wellbeing, passions and interests beyond the classroom as well as applications for Higher Education. Overall responsibility for Sixth Form pastoral care lies with the Director of Sixth Form and Head of LVI, who in turn work closely with the Director of Pastoral Care.
In Sixth Form PSHE (Personal, Social and Health education) pupils are given the opportunity to think about life beyond Queen’s Gate. Sessions are discussion based and include the opportunity to explore female wellbeing, relationships, careers and the future, financial literacy as well as more practical matters such as travel safety and First Aid for undergrads. Suggestions from pupils are always welcome, as we seek to make sure they feel fully ready for the challenges of university and life beyond.

Sixth Form Curriculum
Across the Sixth Form girls will study for three (sometimes four) A Level subjects. Many will also choose to take the Extended Project Qualification which is completed in Lower Sixth (Year 12).
A Levels are challenging courses that require a great deal of independent learning and class engagement. Our small classes ensure girls can feel confident in expressing their views, debating, and respectfully challenging their peers.
All of our offered A Levels are linear courses, meaning assessment of the whole course takes place at the end of Upper Sixth (Year 13).
Guides to Sixth Form
We offer 25 A Level courses, which (subject to demand) can be combined to suit the individual pupil.
Whenever possible, each subject is taught by two members of staff, giving different perspectives on the subject and a mature and independent approach.
A Level Subjects
Classical Civilisation
Courses will run subject to a minimum of two girls
A Level Choices
A full list of A Level choices can be found in the subject sub sections above.

Scholarships & Bursaries
We offer different types of Scholarships from Junior School through to Sixth Form and a number of means-tested Bursaries.
Scholarships

Two scholarships are awarded for entry to Year 3
Each scholarship offers a reduction in school fees and is tenable throughout the top four years in the Junior School.
Applicants will be asked to visit the School and take examinations in English and Mathematics. The Albertopolis Scholarship will be awarded based on results in these examinations, together with an interview with the Principal, and a report from the applicant’s current school.
If you would like to apply for the Albertopolis Scholarship, please contact the Head of Admissions:

Bursaries
We are keen to make a Queen’s Gate education available to as many girls as possible, including those whose families’ financial circumstances might otherwise mean joining us is out of reach. Having benefited from a bursary during her own secondary education, our Principal is proud now to be able to make the same gift to a new generation, and is committed to ensuring that the recipients have an educational experience that mirrors those of our other pupils.
Each year, we are proud to award a limited number of means-tested bursaries to applicants at 11+ and 16+. Bursaries may also occasionally be awarded at other points to relieve hardship where a pupil’s education would otherwise be at risk. These bursaries are worth up to 100% of the value of our school fees, and, where appropriate, will also extend to include school lunches, and some enrichment activities and trips. Please note that applicants for bursaries must have met our normal entry requirements.
Those wishing to apply for a bursary should request the relevant forms from the Head of Admissions and return these by the advertised date, which is usually the penultimate Friday in November. These forms, along with the accompanying supporting information, will then be passed on for means-testing. In this process, a range of factors will be considered, including overall income, dependents, employment status or incapacity to work, investments/significant savings, regular outgoings.
Parents of pupils already at the school, who wish to apply for hardship support, should contact the Bursar in the first instance.
All those awarded a bursary are subject to an annual review, which may consider any or all of the following:
It is also the case that families may be asked to provide information on an annual basis to prove their ongoing financial need for bursarial support. Please note that in the case of selecting whether to offer bursarial support, the decision of the Bursary Committee is final.
